summary_paragraph: A 59-year-old woman with advanced HIV (CD4 count 14), end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, and a history of herpes zoster ophthalmicus presented with worsening right facial pain, new blistering skin lesions, headaches, and dizziness. Initially suspected of shingles reactivation, she was started on antivirals. Workup including CT head, MRI brain, and lumbar puncture showed no evidence of central nervous system infection or acute intracranial pathology. Skin biopsies revealed eosinophilic folliculitis, not herpes, leading to discontinuation of antivirals and initiation of mupirocin cream. Her rash improved, headaches were managed with oxycodone, and desipramine was started for neuropathic pain. She had a brief asymptomatic episode of atrial fibrillation that resolved spontaneously. She completed three hemodialysis sessions with stable parameters. She was discharged home with medication adjustments, suture removal instructions, and follow-up planned with infectious disease, dermatology, and nephrology.
problems: Herpes zoster with other nervous system complications
